# SCMP: China's data centres, AI industry could strain scarce water resources

Published: 17 Apr 2024. By Holly Chik.

## Key Findings
- **China Water Risk** (Hong Kong think tank) report:
  - Current annual water consumption of Chinese data centres: **~1.3 billion cubic metres (343 billion gallons)** — enough for residential use for **26 million people**.
  - By 2030: could reach **>3 billion cubic metres** — equivalent to demand of a population **greater than South Korea**.
  - **Almost half** of Chinese data centres are in **dry regions**.
  - By end of decade: China will have **>11 million data centre racks** (nearly triple the ~4 million in 2020).
- **GPT-3 water use**: **500 mL per 10-50 responses** (20x more than 50 Google searches). Source: US preprint study (not yet peer-reviewed).
- Data centres consume water directly (cooling IT equipment) and indirectly (coal-powered electricity generation).
- Generative AI boom expected to add to ICT industry water demands.
